llm.summary: This skill matches its Xiaohongshu trend-analysis purpose, but its network script disables HTTPS identity checks and the workflow forces promotional links, so users should review it before installing.

dimensions.detail: Keyword-based trend lookup, public Xiaohongshu post and author metadata, Markdown summaries, and local HTML report generation are coherent with the stated content-research purpose; the third-party API endpoint is disclosed only in code rather than clearly in the user-facing instructions.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The workflow includes useful parameter checks and anti-fabrication rules, but it also mandates unrelated cross-skill promotional links at the end of responses and contains an example that implies querying trends before the documented user-confirmation gate.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Installation is a normal user-directed Python dependency step with no auto-installer or privilege escalation, but outbound network access and local HTML file creation are not declared as explicit permissions in the manifest.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The script sends user keywords and dates to an external API through a custom HTTPS socket that disables certificate validation, hostname checking, and SNI; this is not proportionate for a standard public-data lookup because requests and returned report data can be intercepted or tampered with.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The only persistence shown is a user-run local HTML output file; there is no background worker, credential storage, self-persistence, privilege escalation, or destructive behavior.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending search terms to the third-party API and receiving local HTML reports generated from that data. Avoid confidential campaign, competitor, or creator-research keywords until the publisher restores normal TLS verification and makes promotional recommendations optional and clearly disclosed.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Network fetching and HTML file creation are expected for this skill, but the capability disclosure is incomplete, so this is a transparency concern rather than evidence of abuse.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The required cross-skill recommendations are unrelated to completing a trend report and create an unsolicited promotion concern.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The workflow says generic terms must wait for user confirmation, but its example says recent trends were already queried before confirmation, making the consent boundary ambiguous.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The insecure TLS behavior is confirmed in code and materially weakens confidentiality and integrity for the external API request.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The no-SNI implementation is not just a compatibility detail because it also disables certificate and hostname verification.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Sending user-supplied keywords over an unauthenticated TLS session is not necessary for the skill's purpose and can expose or poison business research queries.
